title: Project Manager Salary Melbourne: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Conversion from Hourly to Annual Pay

When you see a job advertisement or receive an offer, it might quote an hourly rate or an annual salary. Converting between the two is straightforward if you know the number of hours worked per week and the number of weeks per year. In Australia, the standard full-time week is 38 hours, and the year is 52 weeks. The formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For example, a project manager salary melbourne advertised at $50 per hour would equate to $50 × 38 × 52 = $98,800 per year. This assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid leave, no overtime, and no penalty rates.

## The 38-Hour Week and the 52-Week Year

The 38-hour week is the standard ordinary hours for full-time employees under most modern awards and the National Employment Standards. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s pay guides confirm that full-time employees work an average of 38 hours per week. When converting an hourly rate to annual, always use 38 hours unless you know your actual weekly hours are different. Part-time or casual employees may work fewer or irregular hours, so the annual figure will vary.

## Fortnightly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the $50 per hour example: weekly pay = $50 × 38 = $1,900; fortnightly pay = $1,900 × 2 = $3,800. This is before tax and any deductions. The [reference tables](/data) on this site can help you check different pay periods.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour or $1,004.90 per week for a 38-hour week. However, many employees are covered by a modern award that sets higher minimum rates. For example, the Clerks—Private Sector Award 2020 (from the Fair Work Commission) has rates ranging from $26.97 per hour for a Level 1 employee to $37.24 for a technical associate. A project manager salary melbourne may fall under a different award or be award-free, so check the applicable award or enterprise agreement. The Fair Work Ombudsman’s Pay and Conditions Tool can help you find the correct rate.

## Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the minimum hourly rate. This loading is meant to compensate for entitlements casuals do not receive, such as paid annual leave and sick leave. If you are a casual project manager, your hourly rate should already include the loading? No – the loading is added to the base rate. When using our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool, enter the base rate (without loading) and check the casual loading box if applicable. The tool will add 25% automatically. For example, if the base rate is $26.44, the casual rate becomes $33.05.

## Superannuation and Tax

Superannuation is paid on top of your gross earnings. From 2026-27, the super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings, up to a maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. So if your annual salary is $98,800, your employer contributes an additional $11,856 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay.

Tax is calculated using the 2026-27 resident tax rates:
- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income between $18,201 and $45,000
- 30% on income between $45,001 and $135,000
- 37% on income between $135,001 and $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Plus the Medicare levy of 2% (with possible reductions for low-income earners). For a $98,800 annual salary, the estimated tax (including Medicare) would be around $22,000, leaving a take-home pay of about $76,800. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a more precise estimate.

## Project Manager Salary Melbourne Context

What does a project manager salary melbourne look like? According to the Australian Bureau of Statistics, full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026, which equates to about $108,352 annually for a 38-hour week. A project manager salary melbourne may be above or below this average depending on industry, experience, and the specific role. For instance, a junior project manager might earn $40 per hour ($79,040 annually), while a senior project manager could earn $70 per hour ($138,320 annually). Always check the relevant award or enterprise agreement, as some project management roles are covered by awards such as the Professional Employees Award or the Clerks Award.

## Important Disclaimer

The annual pay shown here is an estimate based on hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026-27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025-26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026-27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For personalised advice, consult a qualified accountant or use the ATO’s tax calculator.

For more detailed pay rates and allowances, see our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data).
